AI Summary

Three papers this fortnight sit squarely on the lab's bench. Jiang et al. resolve segregating transposable-element alleles as actual sequences across 231 haplotype-resolved human pangenomes with matched long-read multi-omics, moving TE regulatory biology out of the fixed-insertion hindsight that dominates the field and into the polymorphic phase, where they find gain, remodeling and loss all under selection and frequently invisible to gene-level analysis. Courvan et al. show that METTL3 inhibition with STM2457 transcriptionally downregulates the macrophage interferon response through STAT1 — not through altered decay — and leaves THP1 and primary blood macrophages more permissive to coronavirus OC43, which is both a therapeutic angle and a standing confound for any m6A perturbation used to probe TE exonization in immune cells. And Li et al. define TEtrans, a tumor-enriched class of transcripts spliced between TEs with no host gene involved, some acting as oncogenic RNAs and others encoding immunogenic antigens.

The TE-in-cancer thread runs deeper than those two. Hu et al. built an expression atlas of 95,512 individual TEs across 980 subfamilies from roughly 10,000 tumor samples and 1,000 cell lines, nominating 264,252 elements as putative cis-regulatory elements tied to oncogenic programs including MYC activity and inflammatory response — single-element resolution of exactly the kind the LTR10/CRC work depends on, now queryable through their ATEC portal. Pape et al. report HERV-mediated control of calbindin as essential for human early embryogenesis, with non-small cell lung cancer growth depending on cancer-intrinsic calbindin under that same control: the LTR10 logic in another tissue. On the silencing side, Oaks et al. show that replication stress redistributes the H3K9 methyltransferase G9a away from cis-regulatory elements onto stalled forks in a WIZ-dependent manner, de-repressing HBG1/HBG2 — titrating a silencer away from chromatin, rather than removing it, is enough to lift repression.

Viral mimicry gets a structural constraint and two cautions. Thenin-Houssier et al. show by cryo-EM that nuclear cGAS is tethered through the macroH2A1/H2B acidic patch in heterotypic nucleosomes carrying H3K27me3 and H3K9me3, so the very marks that restrain TEs also hold the sensor that would read them; depleting mH2A1.1 releases cGAS and fires cGAS-STING-IRF3. Gao et al. add that nuclear cGAS actively represses LPS-induced primary response genes via HDAC1, independently of STING — so cGAS dosage experiments move a brake as well as a trigger. The cautions: Bashaw et al. find tumor-intrinsic mtDNA instability drives cGAS-dependent melanoma progression, with an early interferon-rich window giving way to immunosuppressive, efferocytosis-skewed macrophages mapping to therapy resistance, and Yan et al. report estrogen-reprogrammed STING driving neutrophil extracellular traps that shield antigen from antibody-drug conjugates. Sustained STING output is not uniformly therapeutic.

On transcript architecture and regulatory variation: Nan et al. map alternative polyadenylation across 2 million brain cells from 379 donors and recover 3'aQTLs for 4,288 genes underlying 168 GWAS loci, only 17.5% shared with eQTLs — the same eQTL-invisible layer that intronic TEs occupy when they drive intronic polyadenylation or premature termination. Bai et al. link single-molecule chromatin state to alternative TSS isoform choice with long-read multi-omics, and Xiao et al. report a B1 SINE inside mouse Malat1 acting as an IRES for micropeptide translation — a TE changing what a transcript does without changing its exons. Two engineered decoy receptors echo the IFNAR2 Alu system: the antibody-lectin chimeras of Stark et al. and the CD24/TGF-β receptor fusion of Cui et al., both binding domains deployed as ligand sinks without signaling output. Rounding out: Das et al. pair a 46,142-enhancer perturbation screen with a deep learning model that recovers cooperative motif grammar, and Mariner et al. find size-associated epigenetic aging in 894 dogs concentrated at transposable elements.
